Simulation-based bound for the first-contrast eigenvalue

Source: R/residual_pca.R
RMdimResidualPCACutoff.Rd

Simulates datasets from a Rasch or partial credit model that fits and resembles your data, and records the largest eigenvalue (the first contrast) of the PCA of standardized residuals in each. Returns several upper percentiles of these eigenvalues. The 99th is the suggested bound for RMdimResidualPCA(), as in RMlocdepQ3Cutoff(). Fixed thresholds do not work, since the eigenvalue depends on the sample size, the number of items and the spread of the item parameters (Chou & Wang, 2010).

Usage

RMdimResidualPCACutoff(
  data,
  iterations = 250,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. Only complete cases are used.

iterations

Integer. Number of simulated datasets. Default 250.

parallel

Logical. Run the simulations in parallel via mirai when it is installed. Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer or NULL. Number of parallel workers. When NULL, getOption("mc.cores") is used. If that is unset too, a warning is given and the simulations run sequentially.

verbose

Logical. Show a progress bar. Default FALSE.

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. See easyRasch2-reproducibility for what this guarantees and how it interacts with parallel.

Value

A list with:

results

data.frame with iteration and eigenvalue.

p95, p99, p995, p999

Percentiles of the simulated eigenvalues.

max

The largest simulated eigenvalue.

suggested_cutoff

The 99th percentile (p99). Pass the whole list to RMdimResidualPCA() as cutoff, or use this value directly.

suggested_cutoff_percentile

The percentile behind suggested_cutoff, always 99.

actual_iterations

Number of simulated datasets that could be used.

requested_iterations

The iterations requested.

sample_n

Number of complete cases used.

item_names

Item names.

Details

The generating model has the CML item parameters (psychotools) and the WLE person locations of data. In each iteration, person locations are drawn with replacement from the WLE estimates, responses are simulated from the model, the standardized residuals are computed with the same engine as for the observed data, and the largest eigenvalue of their PCA is recorded.

A simulated dataset that cannot be refitted, for example because a response category is empty, is left out, and RMdimResidualPCA() reports how many in its caption. actual_iterations gives the number that remained. The iarm package is not needed.

References

Chou, Y.-T., & Wang, W.-C. (2010). Checking dimensionality in item response models with principal component analysis on standardized residuals. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 70(5), 717-731. doi:10.1177/0013164410379322

See also

RMdimResidualPCA()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
dat <- as.data.frame(
  matrix(sample(0:1, 200 * 12, replace = TRUE), nrow = 200, ncol = 12)
)
colnames(dat) <- paste0("I", 1:12)

# Few iterations for a fast example. Use 250 or more in real analyses.
bound <- RMdimResidualPCACutoff(dat, iterations = 50, parallel = FALSE, seed = 1)
bound$suggested_cutoff
#> [1] 1.623358

RMdimResidualPCA(dat, cutoff = bound)
#> 
#> 
#> Table: Rasch model (12 items), n = 200 respondents. Total observed variance: 8.3% explained by measures, 91.7% unexplained. First-contrast cutoff = 1.623 based on 50 simulation iterations (99th percentile).
#> 
#> |Component | Eigenvalue| Proportion of variance|Flagged |
#> |:---------|----------:|----------------------:|:-------|
#> |PC1       |      1.431|                  0.121|FALSE   |
#> |PC2       |      1.407|                  0.119|FALSE   |
#> |PC3       |      1.254|                  0.106|FALSE   |
#> |PC4       |      1.132|                  0.096|FALSE   |
#> |PC5       |      1.105|                  0.093|FALSE   |
# }
